title: Stratified tail-trim bucketing with predictive kernel steering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: In our hosted and dedicated runtimes we observe a long-tail of sequence lengths that causes inefficient GPU utilization due to padding and suboptimal kernel selection. Existing length-bucketing reduces padding but treats all requests in a bucket homogeneously, leading to kernel misalignment (fast kernels used on rare long tails) and conservative prefill/decode schedules that hurt P95 latency under load. Goal: design and implement a stratified bucketing layer that 1) predicts tail/continuation cost per request, 2) steers requests to kernel variants with matching memory/compute characteristics, and 3) applies lightweight tail-trim (depad) heuristics with coordinated prefill/decode scheduling to reduce total padded tokens and preserve SLOs. Scope: runtime-level changes (request router + prefill scheduler + kernel hint API), small model for per-request prediction (budgeted CPU/GPU), kernel affinity table, integration tests, perf benchmarks and gradual rollout on dedicated and hosted clusters.
proposal: High-level design: 1) Runtime intercepts incoming text generation requests and computes a small feature vector: client_hint_len, historical_avg_len (from token metadata), prompt_prefix_entropy, is_streaming, and fast-access token_histogram. 2) A tiny cost predictor (sigmoidal linear model, ~<1KB weights) estimates expected continuation length and tail probability; this runs on request-routing CPU threads. 3) Stratified bucketing: instead of single seqlen buckets, we create stratified bins (short/medium/long + tail-risk high/low). This yields buckets like short-hightail, medium-lowtail, etc., enabling tighter padding without increasing kernel switches. 4) Kernel steering: each stratified bin is mapped to a preferred kernel variant (e.g., fused-attn-fast, memory-saver, block-sparse candidate) using a kernel affinity table populated by offline microbenchmarks. The router emits a kernel_hint in the request proto for the serving engine. 5) Tail-trim & depadding: for high-tail probability requests we apply a conservative tail-trim policy during prefill (trim trailing whitespace/newline tokens and apply runlength-elision heuristics) and allow decode-time dynamic pad-rollback if continuation is short. 6) Prefill/decode schedule: scheduler coalesces prefill operations by bucket and staggers decode lanes to avoid peak memory pressure. Prefill can be preemptively placed on kernels with larger KV capacity while decode uses low-latency kernels. 7) Fallbacks & SLOs: the router monitors a running SLO cost model (latency and token cost); if predictions are uncertain or capacity constrained, the system falls back to conservative single-bucket processing. Offline calibration: an instrumentation job will run per-model microbenchmarks for kernel affinity and produce kernel_latency/cost profiles per sequence length and beam size.
acceptance_criteria: Latency: P95 latency for 512-token median workload must not regress >5% on dedicated clusters compared to baseline.
Cost: Average padded token rate across sampled workloads reduced by >=18% in staging benchmarks.
Correctness: Kernel hints are honored and fallback path executed when hint incompatible; no production failures introduced in rollout window.
Observability: Per-request bucket, kernel_hint, and prediction_score emitted as tags to tracing and console dashboards.
Safety: Feature toggle implements canary rollout and emergency kill switch for new scheduler.
testing_plan: Unit tests for predictor, stratified bucket assignment, and kernel_hint serialization. Integration tests: end-to-end synthetic workloads covering short/medium/long distributions and adversarial tails. Loadbench on dedicated cluster: 8-hour run with mixed workload replay to validate stability. Regression tests: ensure no KV-cache corruption when kernel_hint toggles between requests. Benchmarks: compare staged runtime vs baseline on per-model microbench harness (same harness used for kernel affinity offline runs).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime feature-flag; enable in staging for internal traffic only. 2) Canary: enable on 10% of host shards for non-critical tenant traffic for 48 hours; monitor P95, P99, and padded-token metrics. 3) Expand to 50% with rollback window and automated kill if latency or error rate spikes. 4) Full rollout to hosted clusters and dedicated after 7-day stability. 5) Document kernel-affinity tables and provide SDK flag to opt-out for customers with strict determinism requirements.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Created: initial problem statement and spike planned. Assigned to Luca for prototype.
2025-02-18 - Spike: implemented lightweight predictor prototype (logistic reg + linear) and synthetic harness. Initial predictions correlate with continuation length (r=0.61).
2025-02-25 - Design review: PM and infra reviewed stratified approach. Decided against per-request neural predictor due to CPU budget. Action: build calibration harness for kernel affinity.
2025-03-01 - Implementation: router now emits kernel_hint proto and scoring tag. Added kernel-affinity lookup table in runtime config. Open PR: runtime#8432 (link in design_links).

2025-03-04 - Benchmarks: staging microbench shows padded token reduction of 16% on conversational workload; some P95 regressions (~6%) on long-tail adversarial test. Trade-off: need scheduler tweaks to avoid prefill storms for long-tail buckets.

2025-03-05 - Action items: 1) throttle prefill concurrency per-bucket, 2) add decode-lane backpressure, 3) add canary guard to disable tail-trim heuristics. Assigned to Luca and SRE to implement changes before canary rollout.
Review notes: Design reviewer (Marta Chen) asked for clear metrics and rollback plan; SRE (Diego Alvarez) requested quota for kernel variants to avoid starvation.
